title: printf 串口调试：重定向标准输出（STC）
goal: 掌握无调试器单片机的标准调试手段：实现 putchar 重定向，把 printf 格式化输出经串口发送到 PC 端，实时观察单片机内部变量与运行状态
doc:
为什么需要 printf 调试？

STC89C52 这类单片机没有在线调试器（不能像 PC 程序那样打断点、单步、看变量）。工程师最常用的手段就是把 stdio.h 的 printf 重定向到串口——单片机内部运行情况（变量、状态、分支走向）实时发送到 PC 端串口助手/终端显示，是嵌入式调试的"第一生产力"。

原理：重定向 putchar

printf 内部逐字符调用 putchar 输出。只要自己实现一个"把字符从串口发出去"的 putchar，printf 的所有格式化能力（%d %x %s…）就全部搬到了单片机上：

int putchar(int c) {
    SBUF = c;          /* 字节写入串口发送缓冲 */
    while (!TI);       /* 等待发送完成 */
    TI = 0;            /* 清发送中断标志 */
    return c;
}

接线表（注意交叉！）

USB 转串口适配器单片机
TXDP3.0（RXD）
RXDP3.1（TXD）
VCC / GNDVCC / GND

TXD/RXD 必须交叉接——一方的发送接另一方的接收，这是串口接线最经典的错误点。

操作步骤

  1. 按接线表连接适配器与单片机（双击适配器可设波特率，默认 9600）
  2. 阅读参考代码：uart_init() 初始化串口，uart_putc/puts/putnum 打印三件套
  3. 编译 → 烧录运行
  4. 打开右侧「PC 串口终端」，波特率选 9600，应看到 count 计数持续输出
  5. 修改代码：printf 输出你自己感兴趣的变量（循环次数、按键状态等）

printf 格式速查

占位符含义
%d / %u有/无符号十进制（SDCC int 为 16 位）
%x十六进制
%c / %s字符 / 字符串
\r\n回车+换行（串口输出记得带，否则终端不换行）

思考

1. 为什么 putchar 里要 while(!TI); TI=0;？去掉会怎样？
2. 在中断里调用 printf 安全吗？为什么工程上禁止？

关于标准库 printf（拓展）

真实工程里更常见的写法是重定向 int putchar(int c)，之后直接 printf("count=%d ", cnt)—— printf 内部逐字符调用 putchar，原理与 uart_putc 完全相同（Keil/实物环境推荐此写法）。 本实验采用与 printf 同原理的逐字符发送函数，便于观察串口输出；掌握后可无缝迁移到标准库 printf。 "把字符从串口发出去"的思想一模一样，学会了实物上换 printf 零成本。
checklist: 接线：适配器 TXD→P3.0、RXD→P3.1（交叉！）、VCC/GND 对应连接
理解 putchar 重定向：说出 SBUF、TI 各自的作用
编译烧录后打开 PC 串口终端（9600），看到 count 持续递增输出
改写程序：printf 输出自己感兴趣的变量（如循环变量、模拟状态机状态）
思考题：中断里调用 printf 为什么不安全（提示：putchar 死等 TI 与中断重入）
titleEn: printf over UART: Redirecting Standard Output (STC)
goalEn: The standard debugging method for MCUs without a debugger: implement putchar redirection so printf sends internal variables and status to the PC over the UART, in real time.
docEn:
Why printf debugging?

MCUs like the STC89C52 have no on-line debugger (no breakpoints, single-stepping or variable watches like a PC program). The engineer's favorite technique is to redirect stdio.h's printf to the serial port — the MCU's internal state (variables, status, branch taken) is streamed to a PC terminal in real time. It is the "productivity tool" of embedded debugging.

Principle: redirect putchar

printf calls putchar for every character. Implement a putchar that sends a character out of the UART, and all of printf's formatting power (%d %x %s…) moves onto the MCU:

int putchar(int c) {
    SBUF = c;          /* write the byte to the UART TX buffer */
    while (!TI);       /* wait until the byte is sent */
    TI = 0;            /* clear the TX-complete flag */
    return c;
}

Wiring (mind the crossover!)

USB-UART adapterMCU
TXDP3.0 (RXD)
RXDP3.1 (TXD)
VCC / GNDVCC / GND

TXD/RXD must be crossed — each side's transmit goes to the other's receive. This is the classic serial-wiring mistake.

Steps

  1. Wire the adapter to the MCU per the table (double-click the adapter to set the baud rate, default 9600)
  2. Read the reference code: uart_init() configures the UART; uart_putc/puts/putnum are the three print helpers
  3. Build → flash & run
  4. Open the "PC Serial Terminal" on the right at 9600 — the count should stream continuously
  5. Modify the code to print variables you care about (loop counters, button states, etc.)

printf format quick reference

PlaceholderMeaning
%d / %uSigned / unsigned decimal (SDCC int is 16-bit)
%xHexadecimal
%c / %sCharacter / string
\r\nCR+LF (remember it in serial output, or the terminal never wraps)

Reflection

1. Why does putchar contain while(!TI); TI=0;? What breaks without it?
2. Is calling printf inside an ISR safe? Why is it banned in practice?

About the standard-library printf (extra)

In real projects the common idiom is to redirect int putchar(int c) and then call printf("count=%d\r\n", cnt) directly — printf calls putchar character by character; the idea is identical to uart_putc (recommended on Keil / real hardware). This lab uses character-by-character UART output with the same principle as printf, which also makes each transmitted byte easy to observe; the pattern transfers directly to standard printf on hardware. the idea "send characters out of the UART" is exactly the same, and switching to printf on real hardware costs nothing.
checklistEn: Wiring: adapter TXD→P3.0, RXD→P3.1 (crossed!), VCC/GND matched
Understand putchar redirection: explain the roles of SBUF and TI
After flashing, open the PC serial terminal (9600) and see the count increasing
Modify the program: print a variable you are interested in (loop counter, simulated state, etc.)
Reflection: why is calling printf inside an ISR unsafe? (hint: putchar busy-waits on TI and ISRs can re-enter)
